t: This is St Pancras Hospital, part of North London NHS Foundation Trust, near Camden Town. It specialises in geriatric and psychiatric medicine. Some remarkable people are linked with it. Glyndwr Michael, a Welsh homeless man, died here in 1943, and was later used by British intelligence as the invented Major William Martin in Operation Mincemeat, the Second World War deception sometimes called The Man Who Never Was. Sydney Gibbes, English tutor to the children of Emperor Nicholas II, also died here. Henry Croft, founder of the Pearly Kings and Queens tradition, was born here, and the anarchist David Nicoll died here.
